 Print This week marks the onset of Rama Ekadashi, paving the way for the joyous celebrations of Dhanteras and Diwali, symbolizing prosperity and light. With Venus entering a retrograde phase in Virgo on November 6, financial decisions may require extra caution. While there are no favorable dates for marriage or housewarming, the same day presents a golden chance for buying a new vehicle, enhancing the festive ambiance leading up to Diwali. Rama Ekadashi opens this week with fasting and prayer. Then the focus turns to wealth and light, as Dhanteras falls on Friday and Diwali arrives on Sunday, November 8. On the planetary side, Venus slips back into Virgo on November 6 while moving retrograde. So money matters, home comforts, work quality and daily habits all ask for a more careful hand. No dates suit marriage or Griha Pravesh this week, and property buyers will have to wait too. But Friday, November 6, does offer a sound window for bringing home a new vehicle. All timings follow Indian Standard Time for New Delhi. Shubh Muhurat This Week 
 A Shubh Muhurat comes from reading the Tithi, Nakshatra, weekday, Yoga and Karana together, along with the planetary setting for the task in hand. And a festival date is not automatically right for every big step. Marriage needs its own set of conditions. So does a house move or a vehicle purchase. Vivah Muhurat ·No marriage Muhurat falls in this week. Griha Pravesh Muhurat ·There is no suitable date for Griha Pravesh between November 2 and 8. Property Purchase Muhurat ·Property deals do not get an auspicious window this week. Vehicle Purchase Muhurat This Week Only one slot works for buying a vehicle. ·November 6, Friday: From 10:30 AM, running till 06:37 AM on November 7. Planetary Events This Week 
 Venus changes sign on November 6. ·November 6, Friday at 12:45 AM: Venus enters Virgo. This is the sign of Venus’s debilitation, and the planet is retrograde as well. Spending on luxury may need a second look. Relationships work better with clear, practical talk than with grand gestures. An overlooked EMI date or a pending bill is the kind of detail that tends to surface now. Festivals and Important Observances This Week 
 Diwali week carries deep religious weight across India. ·November 5, Thursday: Rama Ekadashi. Devotees fast and worship Lord Vishnu on Kartika Krishna Ekadashi, and the fast is broken on Dwadashi the following morning. ·November 6, Friday: Dhanteras falls on Kartika Krishna Trayodashi and starts the five-day Diwali festival. Buying gold and silver is a long-held custom on this day. With the vehicle Muhurat landing on the same date, Friday becomes the strongest day of the week for purchases. ·November 8, Sunday: Diwali. Lakshmi Puja is performed on Kartika Krishna Amavasya, the darkest night of the lunar month. Understanding This Week’s Panchanga 
 Every day in the Panchanga rests on five limbs: Vaara, Tithi, Nakshatra, Yoga and Karana. How they combine decides whether a day suits a religious rite or a fresh start. This week runs through the later part of Krishna Paksha, reaching Ekadashi on Thursday and Amavasya by Sunday. The waning Moon is generally treated as weaker for new beginnings. Lord Vishnu also remains in his Chaturmas rest until Devuthani Ekadashi later in November, and that is the main reason wedding and housewarming dates are missing. Vehicle buyers are the exception, with Friday standing out on both religious and Muhurta grounds.
